title: Get started with pyramid_chart
text: command needs long data: one row per category × group. Stata’s bundled pop2000 dataset wide (separate maletotal femtotal columns), reshape first. Two requirements matter: () variable must coded 1 2, value label. Level 1 drawn left, level 2 right, labels become legend. () variable’s value labels become vertical-axis labels, label plotting. Percentages computed within () group: bar category’s share group’s total.
code: sysuse pop2000, clear keep agegrp maletotal femtotal rename maletotal population1 rename femtotal  population2 reshape long population, i(agegrp) j(sex) label define sexlbl 1 "Male" 2 "Female" label values sex sexlbl label variable population "Population" label variable sex "Sex" describe

title: Get started with pyramid_chart
text: three variables number decimals required.

title: Get started with pyramid_chart
text: twoway title option passes straight . dec(1) adds one decimal bar labels; x-axis stays whole numbers.
code: pyramid_chart population, over(agegrp) by(sex) dec(1) ///     title("Population Pyramid for year 2000") subtitle("in percentages") ///     xtitle("Percentage") ytitle("Age groups")

title: Get started with pyramid_chart
text: percentage labels scatter layer. Pass scatter options sctopt().
code: pyramid_chart population, over(agegrp) by(sex) dec(1) ///     title("Population Pyramid for year 2000") subtitle("in percentages") ///     xtitle("Percentage") ytitle("Age groups") ///     sctopt(mlabcolor(blue))

title: Get started with pyramid_chart
text: bar1() bar2() take bar options left right bars respectively, two groups can coloured independently scheme.
code: pyramid_chart population, over(agegrp) by(sex) dec(1) ///     bar1(color(navy%80)) bar2(color(orange%80)) ///     sctopt(mlabcolor(gs4) mlabsize(small))

title: Get started with pyramid_chart
text: everything regular twoway graph, installed scheme applies.
code: pyramid_chart population, over(agegrp) by(sex) dec(1) ///     title("Population Pyramid for year 2000") subtitle("in percentages") ///     xtitle("Percentage") ytitle("Age groups") ///     sctopt(mlabcolor(blue)) scheme(white_tableau) pyramid_chart population, over(agegrp) by(sex) dec(1) ///     title("Population Pyramid for year 2000") ///     xtitle("Percentage") ytitle("Age groups") scheme(economist)

title: Get started with pyramid_chart
text: legend, x-axis labels y-axis labels generated data (x-axis mirrored sides read positive percentages), legend(), xlabel() ylabel() intended changed. Everything else, including name(), saving(), note(), graphregion() xsize()/ysize(), works usual.

title: pyramid_chart: population pyramid charts in Stata
text: pyramid_chart Stata command draws population pyramid: back--back horizontal bar chart showing population distributed across age groups (ordered category) two groups, typically male female. Bars show category’s share group’s total, labelled percentages, axes, legend labels built variables’ value labels.

title: pyramid_chart: population pyramid charts in Stata
text: SSC: manually: download pyramid_chart.ado pyramid_chart.sthlp working directory folder adopath.

title: pyramid_chart: population pyramid charts in Stata
text: data must long format: one row per category × group, numeric value, categorical () variable, two-level () variable coded 1 2 value labels.
code: sysuse pop2000, clear keep agegrp maletotal femtotal rename (maletotal femtotal) (population1 population2) reshape long population, i(agegrp) j(sex) label define sexlbl 1 "Male" 2 "Female" label values sex sexlbl  pyramid_chart population, over(agegrp) by(sex) dec(1) ///     title("Population Pyramid for year 2000") subtitle("in percentages") ///     xtitle("Percentage") ytitle("Age groups")

title: pyramid_chart: population pyramid charts in Stata
text: legend axis labels generated data, legend(), xlabel() ylabel() meant overridden.
code: pyramid_chart varname [if] [in], over(varname) by(varname) dec(#) ///     [bar1(barlook_options) bar2(barlook_options) sctopt(scatter_options) twoway_options]
